summary: Today’s expanded research adds 50 detailed guides and 37 additional screened discoveries across creative AI. Seventeen guides complete earlier screened entries; 70 tools are new to the library. All 500 configured repository queries and 18 model tasks across 64 fields were attempted: one repository query failed and 112 were bounded, so this is broad, disclosed coverage rather than an exhaustive search. Software licenses were reviewed in full for all 87 entries; model, service, asset and proprietary-host terms remain separate. Sixteen unresolved or excluded findings are explained, and Codeberg/SourceHut remain explicit access gaps. These are source reviews, not installations or hands-on demonstrations. Missing independent-use and quality evidence stays visible in the labels. Weekly whole-library review starts October 26 and is not due today.

Package research found phonepod’s local speech-restoration chain. The current Arm ULUNAS model card led to a newly screened MIT upstream speech-enhancement tool; the separate mobile inference package has an early-access dependency and unevaluated accuracy. YoVoice and other audio workflows receive full guides.

Neural rendering, avatar animation, CAD and model inspection remain in scope. Visionary links a hosted editor, but the page could not be opened in this pass; documentation and hardware guidance were reviewed in the source repository. Live primary-paper research on ManifoldSplat supplemented scene-editing discovery. Geometry export is not treated as measured accuracy or fabrication readiness.

Learned painting, procedural shaders and generated typography were covered. The NeuralType author describes a small neural font with important unseen-word failures; this is a finding, not an eligible release claim.

Interactive scene and design authoring were checked through live project documentation, including collaborative agent edits in OpenPencil. Runtime compatibility and output reliability remain workflow-specific.

Text-to-CAD and AI-assisted object design were researched, including CadZero’s official site. Full guides for Fabricator and CAD bridges retain proprietary-host requirements and do not equate STL output with a successful print.

The official Hayao site and playable-example listing document agent-authored 2D games, solver checks and human playtesting. They supplement neural game-model and Three.js authoring research. We reviewed documentation without running the examples; general game quality remains unverified.

The DancingBox paper describes motion capture for digital puppetry; today’s guides add several video-to-motion routes with model and rig limitations. Research origin alone does not produce an Experimental label.

FantasyTalking’s official project page supplements portrait-animation research. Avatar samples, sign dictionaries and motion outputs are described as documented results, not verified communication accuracy or identity preservation.

Current primary model research includes Lightricks’ water-effect IC-LoRA and NVIDIA UniRelight. These model findings are not counted as new eligible software or verified physical simulation.
